messages:
jasper: Heads up — customer ABC Corp seeing spikes of 'context canceled' / 504s after a recent SDK bump. They call /v1/completions; client-side logs show 'net/http: request canceled' and long tails. Quick triage below.
support-bot: Ticket #INC-4321 created for ABC Corp and assigned to support.
maya: Can you paste the minimal client code they're using? Which Go + sdk version? Are they setting http.Client.Timeout or relying on context deadlines?
jasper: Minimal repro from customer:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 8*time.Second)
defer cancel()
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", url, bytes.NewReader(body))
req = req.WithContext(ctx)
client := &http.Client{
    Timeout: 30 * time.Second,
    Transport: &http.Transport{
        MaxIdleConns: 100,
        IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,
    },
}
resp, err := client.Do(req)
if err != nil { log.Println("do err:", err) }
```
maya: Ok — classic mixing of client.Timeout and context timeout. Which Go runtime? Some net/http behavior around cancellation + connection reuse changed between versions.
jasper: Go 1.20.6, go-sdk v0.12.0 (they just upgraded from v0.11.x). Logs show repeated requests stuck waiting, then client-side 'context canceled' and stack traces pointing at net/http. Server side shows no obvious bottleneck.
rafael: We repro locally: with a short ctx (500ms) and client.Timeout larger than ctx we get many sockets in TIME_WAIT / pool exhaustion over time. If client.Timeout==0 and rely only on ctx, behavior is stable. Looks like when ctx cancels, the transport doesn't always cleanly close the underlying connection in this setup.
maya: Workarounds: (A) avoid setting http.Client.Timeout when you already use context.WithTimeout for per-request deadlines (set to 0), (B) set Transport.ResponseHeaderTimeout to something <= your context deadline so the transport will abort waiting for headers, (C) tune MaxIdleConnsPerHost/IdleConnTimeout to avoid conn pool build-up.
jasper: Tried B with the customer: set ResponseHeaderTimeout=5s and MaxIdleConnsPerHost=50. After rolling that change to their client container, error rate dropped ~90% within 10 minutes. Customer confirms fewer 504s.
rafael: I'll open an SDK bug/PR to make the Go SDK construct a sane default Transport when users don't supply one (ResponseHeaderTimeout, MaxIdleConnsPerHost, IdleConnTimeout) and document the hazard of mixing client.Timeout with context. Also add a note to CHANGELOG about go-sdk v0.12.0 -> v0.12.2 fix.
maya: Add a regression test that exercises cancellation + pooled connections across multiple versions of Go (1.19/1.20/1.21) — @eng-runtime FYI, might be an upstream behavior change to track.
eng-runtime: Ack. Assigning to runtime team; will triage with net/http team if needed.
alice: I'll follow up on HTTP2 keepalive/GOAWAY behavior — could also be contributing if the transport tries to reuse half-closed streams.
jasper: Great, thanks all — closing the support loop with the customer and documenting the workaround. :thumbsup:
